title: A writer's task closes on its own work: the plugin's own state is never refused at commit, and an out-of-scope edit becomes a note instead of a refusal
description: Fixes from the stage 1 confirming measurement; the writer's prompt stays equal to plain's.
desiredOutcome: A task whose gate is green commits even when the plugin itself wrote a restore point, and a writer edit outside the task's files is left out of the commit and named, so the measured pipeline can finish a task.

findings.issue: The table matches by path alone, never by content. In this repo .claude/.gitignore and .claude/audit.config.json are TRACKED (git ls-files .claude), so a task's real undeclared edit to either one is now not refused: it is left out of the commit and named in one notes line. Verified by calling split_plugin_owned with project=<root>/sub: '.claude/.gitignore', 'sub/.claude/audit.config.json' and any name under '.claude/audit-backups/' (including a '.py') all go to the named list. The edit is not silent, but the close succeeds with a tracked-file change left uncommitted. The task asked for this on F760 ('if it belongs there'), so it is not a divergence. It is a weaker check than the old refusal for those two files.
findings.resolution: For the two file rows, wave the path only when its change is the plugin's. For .gitignore, that means every added line is one the plugin writes (the ensure_claude_ignored patterns). For audit.config.json, that means the file was absent at the start snapshot. Otherwise keep refusing. At minimum, repeat the plugin-owned line in the refusal output when something else also refuses, so a reader sees what was left out.

findings.issue: The new AUDITED_EXEMPTIONS row is ('live', 'tests/test_commit_task_work.py ctw-at9'). The checker only confirms that the file carries a case id starting 'ctw-at9 ', so the row is well formed and the instrument exists. ctw-at9 pins only the audit-backups and .gitignore rows plus non-empty reasons. The audit.config.json row has no pin: deleting it makes no case red, because ctw-at7 asserts it only through the config edit. The table comment says nothing forces a new writer to add its row.
findings.resolution: Add the config file to ctw-at9's expected paths (os.path.join(root, '.claude', _mio.CONFIG_NAME) in paths), so all three rows are pinned.

findings.issue: The task note and ctx['did'] line say 'the commit carries the declared work' and are written before the re-proof, the re-measured gate and the second commit have run. If the re-measured gate goes red (or the second commit refuses), the paths are already reverted and the note already filed, so the task carries a note claiming a commit the run did not make. The patch path in the note is still correct, so nothing is lost; the sentence is only premature.
findings.resolution: Word the note as what was done ('set aside ... put back to HEAD; the drive asks the commit again') and leave the commit claim to the close line, or file the note after the second commit succeeds.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause: the description says 'Drop the parent's Claude session variables (CLAUDECODE and every CLAUDE_CODE_* / CLAUDE_EFFORT; keep any CLAUDE_* the runner sets on purpose and name them)'. The diff drops a closed list of 14 exact names (PARENT_SESSION_VARS), not every CLAUDE_CODE_*. Any CLAUDE_CODE_* session variable the CLI exports that is not on the list (a new one in a later CLI release, or one the harness list never knew) still reaches the writer, so the writer does not reliably start like a top-level session. The executor's reasoning (a prefix drop would also take CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK and credential switches a plain session inherits) is sound, but it is a narrowing of the clause that the task's own text does not record, and the filed outcome states the narrowing as a design choice rather than a divergence.
findings.resolution: Decide the scope explicitly. Either drop by prefix (CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_EFFORT, CLAUDE_PID, AUDIT_LOCK_TOKENS and every CLAUDE_CODE_*) with a named KEEP tuple for the provider and credential switches (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_*, auth-token names), and add a case with an unlisted CLAUDE_CODE_* name to ras30; or amend the task description to say 'the names run-plain.sh unsets' so the closed list is the asked-for scope. The ras30 decoy for an unlisted CLAUDE_CODE_* name is missing either way, so the closed-list behaviour is untested in both directions.

findings.issue: The comment and the guide say the list is 'the measurement harness's plain arm' list. That harness (run-plain.sh) lives in the private quality-gates-internal repo, not in this one, so a reader of the public tree cannot check the equivalence and nothing keeps the two lists together. I checked it by hand: the 14 names match run-plain.sh lines 62-64 today.
findings.resolution: State the list's basis in this repo (what each name is and why a top-level session starts without it) rather than pointing at a file outside the repository, or add a case that reads a committed copy of the list.

review.outcome: [findings: 5 - 0 high, 1 med, 4 low; 0 with a recorded fix commit]

tasks.title: commit-task-work never refuses the plugin's own state - the manifest restore point under audit-backups/ and the .gitignore line that hides it - and one table of plugin-owned paths is read by both the writer and the check
tasks.description: Register F782. Stage 1 run a2: the gate was green and commit-task-work's undeclared-path refusal (attempt_refusal, commit-task-work.py ~546) refused twice on paths no session created by a tool call: `.claude/.gitignore` gaining `audit-backups/`, then `audit-backups/audit-plan.json.bak-<stamp>`. The writers of those paths are in manifest/_manifest_io.py and migrate-manifest.py (grep audit-backups). Put the plugin-owned state paths (restore points, the .gitignore entry the plugin adds, its state dirs) in one table in a shared module both read; attempt_refusal treats them as plugin-owned: never refused as the task's edit, never silently left out of the record (name them on a line). Check the owner's earlier report of the same class: `.claude/audit.config.json` created mid-attempt was refused too (register F760) - cover it by the same table if it belongs there.

add: tests/test_commit_task_work.py: a task whose attempt left the plugin's restore point under audit-backups/ and the .gitignore line for it commits its own files and names the plugin-owned paths it did not refuse, while an undeclared edit to an ordinary source file is still refused

outcome.technical: NEEDS A SCOPE WIDENING: the new table PLUGIN_OWNED_IN_CLAUDE in _manifest_io.py is a reason-carrying table, so tools/gate-parity.py (exemption_audit_drift) is red on it until a row is added there: in AUDITED_EXEMPTIONS add `"PLUGIN_OWNED_IN_CLAUDE": ("live", "tests/test_commit_task_work.py ctw-at9"),` (proved on a committed copy in /tmp/p135cp.g5uhFM: gate-parity green, its --selftest 93/93). tools/gate-parity.py is not in P135.1.files, so I did not edit it. Changes: (1) _manifest_io.py: constants GITIGNORE_NAME and CONFIG_NAME beside BACKUP_DIR_NAME, the table PLUGIN_OWNED_IN_CLAUDE (name, why) = audit-backups dir, .gitignore, audit.config.json, and plugin_owned_under(claude_dir); ensure_claude_ignored now writes the file named by GITIGNORE_NAME. (2) commit-task-work.py: plugin_owned_rels(project, git_root) places the table under both the project's and the checkout's .claude; split_plugin_owned; attempt_refusal removes those paths from during/predates/undated before asking the refusal question, adds one note line 'plugin-owned state, not the task's edit, left out of this commit and not refused: <path> (<why>); ...', and records attribution['pluginOwned']. Module docstring gains the sentence. They are never staged (not in targets paths), so left out of the commit. (3) tests: ctw-at7 (restore point under audit-backups written by the real ensure_backup_dir + .gitignore line + config edited mid-attempt, beside an undeclared src/img.png: refusal line names img.png alone and no .claude path; after removing img.png the close commits OWNED only, carries no .claude/ path, and names .claude/.gitignore and .claude/audit.config.json as plugin-owned), ctw-at8 (a2's second state: restore point untracked because the ignore line was reverted; close succeeds, names it, does not carry it), ctw-at9 (the restore-point writer's directory and ignore file are rows of the table, each with a reason). Mutations: partition made to treat everything as plugin-owned -> sl1, sl2, ctw-at3, ctw-at5, ctw-at6, ctw-at7 red (129/135); note disabled -> ctw-at7, ctw-at8 red (133/135); both restored, 135/135. Verification on a committed copy (git archive HEAD + my 3 files, own git repo in /tmp): sweep-selftests: 191/194 files ok, red = check-example-ledgers, measure-context, and gate-parity (the missing row above; green with the row); ruff clean; vermin clean. EVIDENCE FROM a2 (<outside-repo>): refusal 1 (drive-state/P125.explain, orchestrator.stream.jsonl line 94): '.claude/.gitignore changed during this attempt and no in_progress task declares it (basis: the snapshot `start` recorded of every dirty path's bytes)'; the orchestrator then ran `git checkout -- .claude/.gitignore`, which made the ignored dir untracked, so refusal 2 (stream line 116): '.claude/audit-backups/audit-plan.json.bak-20261022T100219Z changed during this attempt ...'. Verb: _manifest_io.ensure_backup_dir called from migrate-manifest.py:370 (the layout migration, backup_dir_for at :257) writes both the restore point and the .gitignore line. By timestamp (bak-20261022T100219Z) it was written inside the writer session's whole-tree `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py` run (its Bash call at 09:57:20Z, result back 10:02:27Z; transcripts/875cfdd8...jsonl), not by any listed tool call; the 524-byte restore point reads like a selftest fixture, so a suite that runs the layout migration likely leaked into the real checkout's .claude/ - INFERENCE, not verified, and worth its own fault. F760 (.claude/audit.config.json) is covered by the same table. NOT covered: the plan gate's exemption of .claude/** (hooks/require-plan.py) cannot import scripts/ and does not read this table - F760's 'both read it' half for the gate remains.
outcome.descriptive: A task close no longer refuses on the plugin's own restore point, the ignore line for it or the config file; they are left out of the commit and named, while an undeclared source file still refuses.

tasks.title: On the writer path, an edit outside the task's declared files is left out of the commit and named, instead of refusing the whole task
tasks.description: Register F783. Stage 1 runs a1 and a1b: the writer (plain prompt, which states no scope) edited PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, which the task does not declare; commit-task-work refused the whole task. The writer prompt must stay equal to plain's, so the fix belongs in the drive: on the writer path (executor.writerModel set), before the commit, the drive reverts each undeclared changed path in the task tree after saving it as a patch under the run's state, records a task note naming each path and the patch, re-proves/re-gates if any reverted path was read by the gate, then commits the declared work. Leave the subagent-executor path unchanged (it keeps refusing). Plugin-owned paths (the table from the sibling task) are never reverted.

add: tests/test_drive_phase.py: a writer session that also edited an undeclared file has that file reverted and saved as a named patch, a note names it, and the task commits its declared work; the same edit on the executor path is still refused

outcome.technical: drive-phase.py: close_task on the writer path (writer_path_on and a recorded session) goes through writer_commit: commit-task-work.py as before; on a refusal it is asked again with --json (refusal_answer) and, when the WHOLE refusal is attempt.during paths (no declaredPredates/mixed, undeclared_only), settle_aside runs: paths under _manifest_io.PLUGIN_OWNED_IN_CLAUDE (plugin_owned_paths) or cited by the writer's clause answer (aside_gap, _clause_coverage.check re-read without them) are never reverted - the refusal is relayed with a '[drive-phase] <paths> not set aside: <why>' line; otherwise set_aside writes one binary patch (scratch GIT_INDEX_FILE copy: add -A + diff --cached --binary HEAD, pathspecs via _config.plan_to_git, so the real index is untouched and new files are included) to <stateDir>/set-aside/<phase>/<task>-<utc>.patch, checks it with git apply --check -R, then checks out tracked paths from HEAD and removes created ones; a task note names each path and the project-relative patch; prove_and_hold is asked again (P131.6: re-proves only if HEAD/declared test/impl digests moved, which a set-aside of undeclared paths cannot move); the gate is ALWAYS measured again with no reuse (rerun mark + gate_step), because the ledger records no read set so 'the gate did not read it' has no basis; then the commit is asked once more in text mode. Executor path: unchanged text-mode commit (commit_args/committed_sha factored, same argv). file_writer_return's claim read factored into writer_claim. Module docstring, tree_since_proof docstring and the file_writer_return invariant comment updated. No new import edge (an earlier draft imported _scoped_commit for render, which made _deps.map_drift red against PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md's module map; replaced by relaying the verb's own text). tests/test_drive_phase.py: new block _writer_scope_cases (STAGES row xs-block after wf-block) with xs1-xs6. Gate: python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_drive_phase.py in the task tree -> exit 0, 537 cases. Full sweep on a committed copy (git archive HEAD + the two files, committed in a scratch repo): 192/194 files ok, 16917 cases; red only tools/check-example-ledgers.py and tools/measure-context.py (the two allowed); ruff check plugins/audit tools exit 0; vermin -t=3.8- exit 0. Mutations in a throwaway copy, each red: no regate->xs4; no clause check->xs5; set-aside on executor path too->xs3; plugin-owned guard returns []->xs6; predates/mixed ignored->xs6; no note->xs1,xs2,xs4; declared file also reverted->xs1,xs2,xs4; created file kept->xs1,xs2. DEPENDANTS: tests/test_drive_phase.py - changed (the new block, nothing else). PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md - still correct: drive-phase's import list in the module map is unchanged (no new edge) and no paragraph describes the writer's undeclared-file refusal; README.md, docs/research/pipeline-cost-design.md, docs/research/pipeline-cost-levers.md - still correct, they name drive-phase/its verbs and say nothing about this refusal; plugins/audit/hooks/detect-plan-skip.py, governance/record-risk-confirmation.py, governance/stamp-verification.py, manifest/_areas.py (basename refs) - still correct, the CLI and every existing function signature are unchanged; _carries/_clip/_mark/_marked used by other suites - unchanged. tests/test_drive_phase.py's dependants: .github/sweep-costs.json - still valid (the file runs ~190 s, within its timeout; costs not re-recorded); tests/test__runner_output.py, tests/test_run_test_gate.py (_counting, _follower_cases, _head) - unchanged; tools/sweep-selftests.py - unchanged contract, sb1 stage case green; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, docs/research/* path mentions - still correct. LANDED CONTEXT: P131.6 - prove_and_hold/tree_since_proof asked after the revert, and the gate re-measured, before the commit; P131.7 - a clause cited to a would-be-reverted file is NOT reverted (refusal relayed with the gap), so no clause silently becomes a gap; P132.1 carried commits read by aside_gap via carried_paths; P135.1 PLUGIN_OWNED_IN_CLAUDE read by plugin_owned_paths and never reverted. Waves: a member's undeclared paths stay integrate-task's widen/discard/block decision; this change acts at close_task's commit.

tasks.title: A writer or reviewer session starts as a clean top-level session: run-agent-session does not pass the orchestrator's Claude session variables to it
tasks.description: Found while diagnosing F784: run-agent-session._session_env (~249-253) copies the orchestrator's whole environment, so CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and CLAUDE_EFFORT reach the writer, while a top-level session (and both measurement arms) start without them. Drop the parent's Claude session variables (CLAUDECODE and every CLAUDE_CODE_* / CLAUDE_EFFORT; keep any CLAUDE_* the runner sets on purpose and name them) so a writer starts like a plain top-level session.

add: tests/test_run_agent_session.py: the child environment carries no CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_EFFORT or other CLAUDE_* session variable from the parent, while PATH, HOME and the runner's own variables are kept
